novel_mechanics_found: ls20 is a tuple-matching maze: the player (5x5 two-tone block) carries a hidden (shape, color, rotation/pattern) state shown zoomed in a bottom-left CURRENT display; a boxed glyph elsewhere on the board is the REQUIRED display AND the physical target -- walking into the box with a matching tuple wins the level (it blocks movement otherwise). Discovered this session, on top of the banked L1/L2 knowledge: (1) LAUNCHER STRIPS: 1px color-1 bars embedded in wall edges mark slide pads -- ENTERING the adjacent floor cell auto-slides the player away from the strip to the end of the corridor (free, no extra counter cost); L4 has EIGHT of them forming a one-way expressway system, and slides pass THROUGH other pad cells without chaining. (2) PINWHEEL tile (3x3 quadrant glyph, colors 9/14/8/12): each entry cycles player COLOR in the fixed order C->9->E->8->C. (3) DOTTED PAD (black-dot glyph cell): each entry MORPHS the displayed shape/pattern -- on L3 it acted as a 90-degree-CW rotator; on L4 it cycles distinct shapes (S-shape -> the 6-cell target shape -> others), so shape AND rotation are set here. (4) STEP COUNTER (bottom HUD bar): drains per action -- 2/move on L3, 1/move on L4; blocked moves still drain; at 0 the NEXT action restarts the level (fresh counter/rings/color/shape/position) and consumes one of three 588 life tokens (tokens restore on level-up). (5) B-RING pickups reset the counter to 42; consumable, restored on restart. GOTCHA: the B-ring-lookalike at the bottom of L4 (r51-53 c31-33) did NOT reset the counter when stepped on -- unknown function.
narrative: Replayed the banked 58-label prefix to L2, then solved L3 (96 further actions incl. exploration and one deliberate counter-death to learn restart semantics): color via pinwheel, rotation via the dotted pad, counter via both rings, then entered the 9-glyph box -- the level completed with 2 counter to spare. L4 is a much larger one-way maze built from eight launcher expressways; after mapping it cell-by-cell and discovering the pad also morphs SHAPE on this level, a first attempt died when the bottom ring failed to fire, but the death was converted into a planned restart and a 47-move optimal line (3 pinwheel entries, 1 pad entry, ring1 collected with exactly 1 counter left) won L4. The full 244-label line (including the embedded death-restart) reproduced from a fresh reset: reproduced=True at claimed_level=4. Stopped there: 488/500 env steps used -- no budget left to explore L5.
gotchas: Counter drain rate is level-specific: 2 per action on L3, 1 per action on L4. Blocked moves drain too.

Counter at 0: the NEXT action triggers a level restart (not immediate), consuming one 588 life token; 3 tokens per level, restored on level-up. Restart restores rings, counter, color, shape, and start position.

Launcher slides trigger on ENTERING the strip-adjacent cell (arrival, not press), slide away from the strip to the corridor end, cost only the entering action, and do NOT chain through other pad cells.
Pinwheel color cycle order is C->9->E->8->C, one step per entry, entry direction does not matter (only tested N entries).
The dotted pad is not a pure rotator on L4 -- it cycles SHAPES (S -> target-shape -> [XX./.XX/X.X] -> ...); plan exactly one entry from the fresh S state to hit the target shape.
The bottom-left boxed glyph is the CURRENT tuple display; the required tuple is drawn inside the target box itself (glyph color = required color).
L4 bottom B-ring lookalike (r51-53 c31-33) did NOT reset the counter when stepped on -- treat only verified rings as refreshes when planning counter budgets.
The ls20 L4 winning line has near-zero counter slack: ring1 (r16-18 c20-22) must be collected on the FINAL approach (arrive with 1 counter left), not early.
